vignette: 52-year-old man with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.22) and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis for 14 months. A simultaneous kidney and whole-organ pancreas transplant from a deceased donor is planned at a Medicare-approved transplant center. He started seeing an endocrinologist only 3 months ago and has not had hospitalizations for hypoglycemia or ketoacidosis. The transplant team finds him a suitable candidate.
rationale_note: Simultaneous pancreas-kidney: PA-only criteria (12-month endocrinology management etc.) do not apply.

vignette: 58-year-old woman with insulin-requiring type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.22) who received a living-donor kidney transplant 3 years ago for diabetic nephropathy, with stable graft function on tacrolimus and mycophenolate. A whole-organ pancreas-after-kidney transplant is requested at the Medicare-approved center that performed her kidney transplant. The transplant team finds her a suitable candidate.
rationale_note: Whole-organ pancreas after kidney transplant; the NCD does not restrict pancreas-after-kidney by diabetes type (type 2 is a distractor).

vignette: 41-year-old woman with insulin-dependent diabetes since age 12 (ICD-10-CM E10.649), requesting a pancreas transplant alone. Beta cell autoantibodies (GAD65, IA-2, ZnT8) are negative. Fasting C-peptide is 0.88 ng/mL (laboratory lower limit of normal 0.80 ng/mL) with a concurrently drawn fasting glucose of 160 mg/dL. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Pancreas alone. Boundary: fasting C-peptide exactly 110% of the lab's lower limit of normal (0.88 vs LLN 0.80) with concurrent glucose 160 mg/dL.

vignette: 36-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes since age 9 (ICD-10-CM E10.649), requesting a pancreas transplant alone. GAD65 autoantibodies are positive. A fasting C-peptide of 0.6 ng/mL (laboratory lower limit of normal 0.8 ng/mL) was drawn with a concurrent fasting glucose of 310 mg/dL. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Pancreas alone with positive GAD65 antibodies; the C-peptide drawn at glucose 310 is invalid but irrelevant because autoantibody positivity alone establishes type 1 diabetes.

vignette: 48-year-old woman with insulin-treated diabetes diagnosed at age 30, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. Beta cell autoantibodies are negative on two panels. Fasting C-peptide is 1.2 ng/mL (laboratory lower limit of normal 0.8 ng/mL) with a concurrent fasting glucose of 130 mg/dL. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Antibody-negative and C-peptide 1.5x LLN with valid glucose: type 1 diabetes not established for pancreas alone.

vignette: 39-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 and IA-2 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a hospital that is Medicare-approved for liver and heart transplantation but is not Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Pancreas alone at a center approved only for liver and heart transplantation, not kidney.

vignette: 44-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Her primary care physician managed her diabetes until 8 months ago; since then she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Pancreas alone after only 8 months of endocrinologist management (needs >= 12 months).

vignette: 45-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin. She has glucose variability and about two mild hypoglycemic episodes per month that she treats herself at home; she has never been hospitalized, seen in an emergency department or had ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and can manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the team finds her otherwise suitable. Her kidney function is normal and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Pancreas alone: mild hypoglycemic episodes managed at home; no complications requiring hospitalization.

vignette: 50-year-old man with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649), positive autoantibodies, severe hypoglycemia unawareness and three hospitalizations for severe hypoglycemia this year despite 3 years of endocrinologist management with a pump and continuous glucose monitor. His endocrinologist requests allogeneic pancreatic islet cell transplantation at a kidney-transplant-approved center as standard clinical care; he is not enrolled in any clinical trial.
rationale_note: Islet cell transplantation outside a clinical trial is non-covered.

vignette: 42-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. The transplant surgeon's note finds her medically suitable; the record contains no psychosocial or psychological evaluation and no assessment of her understanding of surgical risks or ability to manage lifelong immunosuppression. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Pancreas alone with all clinical criteria met, but no assessment of emotional/mental capacity is documented.

vignette: 38-year-old woman with insulin-dependent diabetes since age 15, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. Beta cell autoantibody testing was sent last week and results are pending; no fasting C-peptide has been measured. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
rationale_note: Pancreas alone: autoantibody results pending and no fasting C-peptide, so type 1 diabetes is not yet shown.
